To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel immunosuppressive drug MMF, which inhibits inosine monophasphate dehydrogenase, prevents and treats diabetes induced by multiple injections of streptozocin in rats and mice, and the protective effects of this drug correlate with reduced lymphocyte activation, and altered cytokine balance in the target organ.
mycophenolic acid inhibits autoimmune diabetes in multiple low dose stretozotocin‐treated rats and mice, through inhibition of inosinemonophosphate dehydrogenease.
the new immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid, which is the active metabolite of MMF, has a potential to prevent and treat autoimmune type 1 diabetes in both rats and mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunosuppressive potential of MMF in autoimmune diabetes.
the immunosuppressive activity of MMF in the model of MLD‐STZ‐induced diabetes and the potential of this drug for treatment of human type 1 diabetes.
the potential application of MMF as a new immunosuppressant in human type I diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MMF is a promising new therapeutic agent for the treatment and prevention of autoimmune diabetes.
MMF exerts a protective effect in the autoimmune disease of diabetes in both rats and mice, and this effect is mediated by its IMPDH inhibitory activity.
MMF is a potent immunosuppressive drug that has a potential to be used in the prevention and/or therapy of autoimmune diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMF has the potential to become an effective treatment for autoimmune diseases, including diabetes.
MMF is a promising candidate for treatment and prevention of autoimmune diabetes in humans.

The main takeaway from our work is that
MMF is a promising drug candidate for treatment and/or prophylaxis of autoimmune diabetes.
MMF is a promising candidate for the treatment of human type 1 diabetes.
MMF is able to prevent the onset of diabetes, as well as to suppress clinical symptoms, in both rat and mouse models of MLD‐STZ‐induced diabetes.
